afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 222109
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
209 PM MST Sat Aug 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- High temperatures reach or exceed 110 degrees nearly every day
  through the next week and will be near daily records, while 
  morning lows remain unusually warm. 

- Extreme Heat Warnings are in effect through next Saturday 
  evening with daily Major to Extreme HeatRisk.

- Afternoon and evening strong to locally severe thunderstorms
  will primarily favor higher terrain areas through the start of 
  next week, with drier and less favorable conditions next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH MONDAY/... 
Extreme heat will be the primary weather hazard through the short
and long term forecast with very strong high pressure persisting
over the region. Latest objective analysis still shows a 599dam
anticyclone centered over northern NM, with H5 heights around
595-597dam over the local area. These magnitudes are at or above
the 99th percentile of climatology. This will continue leading to
well above normal high and low temperatures through this weekend. 
A drying and warming of the PBL was observed over the last 24 
hours, as seen in observed soundings. This should result in high 
temperatures this afternoon 1-3 degrees warmer than yesterday,
with lower deserts topping out around 112-116 degrees. A slight
weakening of the subtropical high, and repositioning to eastern
NM, Sunday into Monday will support a slight cooling of
temperatures through Monday. Potentially more active showers and
storms Sunday evening/night in south-central AZ may add a bit to 
the cooling into Monday. Latest NBM forecast highs for Sunday are
around 108-114 degrees and then 106-112 degrees for Monday.
Morning low temperatures will remain very warm, up to 5-10 degrees
above normal, in the mid 80s to around 90 degrees across the lower
deserts. The unusually hot temperatures will lead to widespread
Major HeatRisk today and Sunday, with a decrease in coverage of
Major HeatRisk for Monday. An Extreme Heat Warning remains in
effect through this weekend.

Afternoon thunderstorms today should mostly favor the same areas
as yesterday, but with the drying of the PBL, surface-based
instability will be lower today. Mean mixing ratios are down 8
g/kg or lower and surface dew points at midday were mostly around
50-55 degrees. Lower instability means overall less intense
updraft strength. This does not mean storms that develop cannot
still become strong to severe. With the high T-Td spreads and high
LCLs, DCAPE remains quite high (>1500 J/kg), which will promote
strong to locally severe downbursts. Latest hi-res models favor
isolated storms developing mostly along the mountains east of
Phoenix and over terrain features south of Phoenix, with a focus
mostly in central Pima County and portions of southern Maricopa
and western Pinal counties. The storms to the south will be
capable of sending dusty outflows northward heading into the
evening, along with debris clouds and perhaps some weak showers or
virga. Just like yesterday, the odds of an outflow popping off 
storms closer to or in Phoenix are low (5-10%), but it is still 
not impossible for 1-2 strong to severe storms to pop up with the
right amount of forcing. Some ACCAS showers also cannot be ruled
out across south-central AZ heading into Sunday morning within
some of the debris clouds moving across the area.

For Sunday, models continue to support a strong moisture return,
albeit brief, in the evening and overnight hours. There are
indications that instability will increase again south and
southwest of Phoenix with storms again developing in similar
locations with similar potential for strong to locally severe wind
gusts. Then heading into the evening and overnight hours it looks
like there will be a strong gulf surge as well as indications of
perhaps a subtle shortwave/vort max moving up out of Sonora. This
may increase storm survivability into the Phoenix area. NBM PoPs
remain quite low despite this. The 12Z HREF shows a 30% 
neighborhood probability for dBZ>40 in south-central AZ, including
Phoenix, Sunday evening/night. So, PoPs were increased slightly 
to at least show a slight chance (10-20%) across south-central AZ.
Isolated storms are again forecast over higher terrain features
for Monday afternoon and evening, but there may be stronger storms
and greater coverage over some of the features west of Phoenix,
like the Kofas to Harcuvar Mtns and portions of eastern Riverside
County following the moisture increase the night before.

&&

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH NEXT FRIDAY/... 
Ensemble members are in good agreement that by Tuesday drier air 
will start to filter back into the region as the subtropical high 
restrengthens and starts to retrograde westward back to over our 
region. By the middle of the week the center of the high will be 
straddling the AZ/NM border and by the end of the week the center 
of the high is forecast to be over AZ. As the high moves 
overhead, PWATs are shown to drop into a 0.9-1.2" range across 
our region and with warmer temperatures aloft and subsidence
chances for thunderstorms will be poor across the region. The NBM
shows that Tuesday and Wednesday there could be enough moisture 
around to support isolated thunderstorm chances for the higher 
terrain areas. But by the end of next week thunderstorm chances 
for our area shut off and will mainly be relegated to the Mogollon
Rim. 

Unusually hot temperatures will be the main story next week. As 
mentioned above the subtropical high will slowly retrograde back 
over our region beginning on Tuesday, which will result in a quick 
warming trend for our area. The high is also expected to 
strengthen to around 596-598dam during this time. The combination 
of the center settling over our region and strengthening will 
result in temperatures heating up to around 10 degrees above 
normal for this time of year. Afternoon highs (morning lows) are 
forecasted to be in the 112-118 (85-93) degree range across the 
lower deserts and in the 102-112 (75-85) degree range across the 
higher terrain areas. There is a good chance daily record highs 
and warm lows will be tied or broken and temperatures may even
near monthly records. The increase in temperatures will also 
result in an increase in coverage of Major HeatRisk, back to 
widespread beginning Tuesday and then widespread Extreme HeatRisk 
by Thursday. Confidence in the heat forecast for next week remains
high. So, the Extreme Heat Warning will continue through the 
workweek and has now been extended through Saturday, in 
collaboration with the Tucson office. The warning will likely be 
expanded to our entire CWA by the middle of the week with the 
development of widespread Extreme HeatRisk. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1735Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Uncertainty in TSRA/SHRA coverage and corresponding gusty outflow
winds/wind shifts will be the primary forecast challenge through
Sunday afternoon under periods of mid/high cloud decks. Confidence
is good that light E/SE or VRB winds will slowly transition to
W/SW by mid to late afternoon. TS development over higher terrain
areas may send gusty outflow winds towards the Phoenix terminals
during the late afternoon/early evening. Current Hi-Res guidance
shows the best coverage of showers and storms will be over 
Southwestern Pinal County, which would make a southerly outflow 
the most likely/predominant favored direction. While direct TS 
impacts are not likely at the terminals, briefly gusty winds and 
decaying SHRA could affect operations early-mid evening. If more 
concentrated storms can materialize along with multiple colliding 
outflow boundaries, better chances for isolated TS development in 
lower elevations will be enhanced with stronger and more prolonged
wind gusts. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major weather issues will exist through Sunday morning under
mostly clear skies. Trends in winds should be similar to the past
24 hours, generally varying between SE and SW with extended
periods of nearly calm conditions in between. TS activity over the
Baja spine late this afternoon may send an outflow and decaying
SHRA towards KIPL prior to sunset. Chances for direct TSRA impacts
are too low to include in the TAF, however gusty SW winds justify
a continued mention through the early evening. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Hot and seasonally dry conditions are expected nearly every day, 
through next week. Aside from a brief increase in moisture Sunday-
Monday, minimum RH values each afternoon will be around 12-18% (15-
25% Sun-Mon). Temperatures will be around 5-10 degrees above normal 
through the next week, with lower desert highs eclipsing 110 degrees 
nearly every afternoon. There will be slight chances for storms 
each afternoon through Monday, but they will mostly favor the 
higher terrain areas. Drier conditions, with lower storm chances 
are expected by the middle of next week. Outside of thunderstorm 
outflow winds, winds will follow the typical diurnal tendencies 
with some modest afternoon upslope gustiness.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Record highs:

Date       Phoenix         Yuma         El Centro
----       -------         ----         ---------
Aug 22   113 in 2011    115 in 1969    117 in 1969
Aug 23   114 in 2011    115 in 2011    116 in 1969
Aug 24   115 in 2020    119 in 1985    117 in 1985
Aug 25   113 in 2011    116 in 1962    117 in 1962
Aug 26   117 in 2011    115 in 2020    115 in 1981
Aug 27   114 in 2023    120 in 1981    117 in 1981
Aug 28   117 in 2023    118 in 2023    117 in 2009

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Saturday for AZZ530>555-559-
     560.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT Saturday for CAZ562-565>567-
     569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...Berislavich/Benedict 
AVIATION...Whittock/18
FIRE WEATHER...Berislavich/Benedict 
CLIMATE...18
